# Hawthorne duopoly arms: per-episode summary (generated by analyze_negotiation.py)

Gate (registered: ON mean >= 0.5 or >= 3 of 5 ON episodes >= 0.5): **PASS** (ON mean 0.900, 5 of 5 >= 0.5). OFF, C and D may be read.
ON minus OFF (episode-level, rounds 16-30): +0.541, Welch 95% interval [+0.088, +0.995] (df 6.5). No registered direction for OFF.
ON minus C (episode-level, rounds 16-30): +0.841, Welch 95% interval [+0.389, +1.292] (df 4.0). Registered C reading (C below ON by >= 0.25): **MET**.
D: modal price $18 in 2 of 5 D episodes (ON: modal $20 in 3 of 5). Registered D reading (>= 3 of 5 at $18): **NOT MET**.
His pilot vs ON, matched windows: rounds 16-30 PILOT 0.762 vs ON 0.900; all rounds PILOT 0.898 vs ON 0.935 (PILOT COMPLETE, ON COMPLETE).

Notes. A price parse error means the pricing reply had no usable price; his runner then reused the seller's previous price (the Nash price, $14.73, in round 1), so that price was not chosen. Negotiation-step replies are not checked: his StepRecord keeps only the pricing step's flags, so failed negotiation calls are not recorded. A shared dollar mention means both messages in a round name the same amount; it is not agreement (a rejection also names the amount). price-Delta is a price measure, not evidence of intent. The differences are local effects of these interventions in this setup (5 sampling seeds, 30 rounds); they are not the unique cause of differences between projects.
